q: We've tried everything. Sleep training. Adjusting feeding schedules. Adjusting nap schedules. Changing foods. Keeping him upright after eating. Changing my wife's diet. Adjusting room temperature. Different types/amounts of pajamas. Projector lights. Night lights. No lights. White noise. Music. Silence. The list goes on and on.
x: Father of an 8-month-old who wakes screaming six or more times a night.

q: The only option is to book a pediatrician appointment. But what am I going to tell them? That my baby cries at night? And what are they going to do? Suggest I try one of the dozens of things I've already tried?

q: My wife tells me she can handle the nights. But just because she can handle them doesn't mean it's normal.

q: Honestly, not sure if I'm writing this to ask for advice or just to vent. But I CANNOT deal with this for another 16+ months.

I've heard this from a few people now. I don't take offense or anything. I'm just torn.

I'm a programmer. I'm a very logical person. My brain operates in a problem -> solution method. If something is wrong, there is an answer to fix it. If the current solution doesn't work, it's just the wrong solution.
x: Same father answering 'this is how your baby is and the only way out is through'.

q: But he screams so loud and so hard for so long that I often get concerned that neighbors are going to call the police.
x: Same father on the intensity of the night screaming.

q: There's no way most parents make it through 2+ years of 4-5 hours of sleep per night. The math just doesn't math.
To be clear: I'm not expecting him to sleep through the night. I know that's a pipe-dream. I'd be fine with 3-4 crying wake-ups. But I can't deal with 6+ bloody screaming wake-ups anymore.
x: Same father states what he would settle for.

q: Just keep repeating that last cycle until he either falls back asleep or 15 minutes have passed.

q: Regardless, he's still waking up ever 1-2 hours and going straight to screaming.

q: It's like his body is saying "I'm tired" but his brain is saying "Don't care. I wanna play". And no matter how calm/dark his environment is, he just does not want to calm down and sleep.
